title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery (Lyra Solutions)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Lyra, HoP), Ben Ortiz (Lyra, Eng Lead), Maya Rivera (Lyra, Security)

Summary (auto): quick intro to Redwood PLG quickstart, discussion of hosted vs dedicated vs private, how free credits and time-to-first-token work, security questions (SOC2/KMS/SSO), next steps to try quickstart and schedule deeper SE demo.

Topics: quickstart flow; free credits; time-to-first-token; hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private; VPC/KMS/SSO; benchmarks & cost tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy new year, um, we'll do a quick 45 minute discovery, intro to our PLG quickstart, show how to get tokens and answer security questions. Ethan's going to jump in on the technical bits.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Thanks Sofia, yeah excited, we want to see how quickly our small team can go from sign-up to first inference. Typical goal is time-to-first-token within a day and simple SDK.
[00:24] Ethan Chen: Great, that's exactly the fast path we built for. Quick overview — Redwood has a hosted API for self-serve, we also offer Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. The quickstart is focused on the hosted flow: you sign up, get free credits, run sample calls, and integrate the SDK in a few minutes.
[00:40] Ben Ortiz: Quick q, when you say free credits, is that tied to a card? We prefer not to have cards for initial trials.
[00:48] Sofia Martinez: Good question. We usually offer initial credits that can be applied to an account without a card, depending on program. For customer pilots we can provision partner credits or a promo token. I'll follow up with a link and a redemption code.
[01:05] Maya Rivera: From compliance side — what logging do you provide? Audit logs and retention? Also SOC2?
[01:12] Ethan Chen: We provide request-level audit logs in the Console, and we have SOC 2 Type II attestation. For Private or Dedicated we can optionally push logs to your SIEM, and control retention. We also integrate with KMS providers for customer-managed keys.
[01:28] Aisha Khan: And SSO? Our product folks want SCIM and SAML for RBAC.
[01:33] Sofia Martinez: Yep, SAML/SCIM is supported. We'll share our security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary) after the call.
[01:42] Ben Ortiz: Back to the quickstart — what's the realistic time-to-first-token for an engineer who has never used Redwood?
[01:47] Ethan Chen: If you follow the quickstart it's ~10-30 minutes to get a token and run a basic text generation. SDKs are in JS/Python. The common delays are org provisioning or SSO setup but for individual devs it's very fast. In practice we've seen customers onboard the first dev within the hour.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: Nice. For our use case we're prototyping an in-app assistant, lower latency matters for interactive UX. Can you share latency numbers for hosted?
[02:14] Ethan Chen: Hosted latency depends on model and sequence length. For smaller models and short prompts we often see P95 under 200ms; for larger context or long generations it's more. If you need consistent low latency at scale, Dedicated with pinned GPU pools is typical. We can share benchmark sheets for similar workloads.
[02:33] Ben Ortiz: Are there autoscaling guarantees on Dedicated? We have bursty traffic patterns.
[02:38] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated offers configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options — SLAs are available on reserve contracts. For prototyping you can start hosted and then move to Dedicated as you mature.
[02:50] Maya Rivera: For Private deployments, does Redwood require hardware procurement or do you provide an on-prem package?
[02:56] Ethan Chen: We support an on-prem package as well as customer-managed private deployments into your VPC. On-prem has extra ops lift but can be air-gapped. We also provide a private control plane option for enterprises.
[03:08] Aisha Khan: Can we run some small benchmarks during a trial? We want to compare cost/latency with our current self-hosted setup.
[03:14] Ethan Chen: Absolutely — typical POC steps: 1) run quickstart on hosted to validate functional flow, 2) run a small benchmark using our sample harness (we'll provide the script), 3) if Dedicated is desired we can provision a short-term Dedicated node for throughput tests.
[03:30] Ben Ortiz: How do you handle prefix caching or KV cache when switching models? We use a lot of chat workloads.
[03:36] Ethan Chen: We have automatic KV cache management and prefix caching to optimize token costs for conversational workloads. It works across model variants when compatible, and runtime will fallback gracefully to compatible variants when needed.
[03:48] Aisha Khan: Any gotchas with tokenization differences across models?
[03:51] Ethan Chen: Good call — tokenization differences affect costs and truncation. Our SDK includes token counters and cost estimates. We'll help pick a recommended model/quant profile for your workload.
[04:04] Sofia Martinez: On pricing — hosted is usage-based (per-token, per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. For pilots, we typically share a rough estimate and then refine it after a short benchmark.
[04:18] Ben Ortiz: Competitors — we also eval OpenAI and HF Inference. How do you compare on price?
[04:24] Sofia Martinez: It's workload dependent. We often win on cost when batching, caching and custom quantization profiles are used. We'll run a quick cost estimate once you share sample prompts.
[04:36] Maya Rivera: Security again — can you sign our DPA and support data residency in EU?
[04:41] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we have DPA templates and support regional deployments. For EU residency we run in specific cloud regions and we can discuss contract terms.
[04:50] Ethan Chen: Also note — for Dedicated/Private we can enable customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; for hosted we integrate with major KMS providers for key wrapping in enterprise tiers.
[05:04] Aisha Khan: What are the common blockers you've seen for teams adopting Redwood?
[05:09] Sofia Martinez: Mostly procurement and security reviews for larger orgs, and sometimes latency or model choice for product teams. But for PLG/self-serve teams the friction is minimal — credits and docs usually get the first dev productive quickly.
[05:22] Ben Ortiz: Ok can we get a sample quickstart link and a CLI example?
[05:26] Sofia Martinez: Yeah I'll send the quickstart guide and a code snippet, plus a sandbox token. Link: https://www.redwood.ai/quickstart (note: internal link)
[05:36] Aisha Khan: If we try quickstart and like it, what's the next step to move to Dedicated?
[05:41] Sofia Martinez: After you validate functionally we can scope a Dedicated pilot — usually a short contract to provision reserved capacity for load testing, then long-term commit. We'll put together a proposal.
[05:53] Ethan Chen: For the technical demo we can run a 30-45 minute session where we reproduce your typical user flow and run latency/cost numbers.
[06:02] Maya Rivera: We also need to see SOC2 report and your vulnerability scan summary before procurement moves forward.
[06:08] Sofia Martinez: Understood, we'll include the security pack in our follow-up.
[06:13] Ben Ortiz: Anything else on integration? Webhooks for async responses?
[06:17] Ethan Chen: We support streaming responses and webhooks for async patterns. SDKs hide the complexity for you.
[06:24] Aisha Khan: Great, let's recap next steps.
[06:28] Sofia Martinez: Recap — I'll send quickstart guide, free credits token, security pack, and sample benchmark script. Ethan will schedule the technical demo next week. Lyra will try the quickstart and share sample prompts and a small dataset for cost/latency estimate.
[06:44] Ben Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks Sofia, Ethan.
[06:47] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, speak soon.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription, some speaker overlap and minor mis-hears (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cache'), product names occasionally mis-capitalized.
